# Question: generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **column span only**:

```text
output width = abs(column_2 - column_1) + 1
```

It fits the two canonical demonstrations that act as training examples: the
horizontal pair has width 5 and the diagonal pair also has column span 5. It
fails on the canonical vertical case and on this exact generated input:

The intended inclusive Chebyshev span is 7, so the selected Racket rule returns
`[[8,8,8,8,8,8,8]]`; the shortcut returns `[[8]]`. I checked the intended
output with the supported command recorded in
`checks/main-counterexample/racket-final.json`, which binds executed rule hash
`5661890ac5fd`, final generator SHA-256
`7ce8cf77ecf3c7c034ac0b5054e6735b54a5a4f3dfeff1e2b49b98118f95e414`,
and the exact input/output hashes.

Yes, the repaired generator emits this case: seed 31, sample index 5, with exact
overrides `orientation="vertical"`, `segment_length=7`, and
`endpoint_color=2`. More generally, the six-slot alternating schedule makes
every four-pair default lesson contain two vertical examples, so any one-pair
query holdout leaves at least one demonstration that refutes the shortcut. The
default period also contains both diagonal directions.
